results.title: Bronkhorstspruit residents face worsening water crisis amid Tshwane restrictions
results.description: Bronkhorstspruit residents face worsening water crisis amid Tshwane restrictions Estelle. Bronkhorst Thu, 11/19/2026 - 08:50 BRONKHORSTSPRUIT - With Level 2 water restrictions now in effect across Tshwane, residents have been urged to conserve water and reduce their consumption. But for many Bronkhorstspruit residents, who have endured decades of unreliable water supply, the restrictions are adding to an already desperate situation. Some residents have resorted to collecting water from a nearby stream for household use while waiting for municipal water tankers to arrive. READ: Bronkhorstspruit residents still waiting for clean water Residents are still waiting for assurances that clean, safe drinking water will be restored to their taps. During a briefing on 20 October, government officials -- including the water and health ministers -- promised that residents would have access to clean drinking water within days. However, almost a month later, the situation remains unresolved. Residents continue to rely on alternative water sources and municipal tankers for their daily needs. READ: Tshwane residents face fines for failing to comply with water restrictions Meanwhile, Tshwane is warning that residents who fail to comply with the water restrictions could face fines of up to R5,000. The municipality says water consumption is exceeding targets and that Rand Water’s storage systems are under pressure. The restrictions include limiting water use for gardens and swimming pools, as well as discouraging unnecessary water consumption.

results.title: Groups rally outside MPD, demand release of 9 activists
results.description: Progressive groups staged a protest outside the Manila Police District (MPD) headquarters along United Nations Avenue in Ermita, Manila, on Thursday, Nov. 19, condemning the arrest of nine activists during anti-ASEAN demonstrations last Sunday, Nov. 15. Around 25 protesters from Kilusang Mayo Uno (KMU), Alliance of Concerned Teachers (ACT), Youth Act Now Against Tyranny (YACAP), Makabayan Bloc, PISTON, and the College of Arts and Sciences Student Council of the University of the Philippines Manila (CAS-UPM) joined the demonstration, which started at 12:05 p.m. and ended at 1:15 p.m. MPD Spokesperson Maj. Philipp Ines said police remained open to dialogue and expressed confidence that the situation could be settled through peaceful discussions. “Walang bagay ang hindi naidadaan sa maayos na usapan at bukas na kaisipan (There is nothing that cannot be resolved through proper dialogue and an open mind),” Ines said. Among those who joined were KMU chairperson Jerome Adonis, Makabayan president Liza Maza, ACT chairperson and former congresswoman France Castro, Rep. Antonio Tinio, Rachelle Junsay, Ka Mimi Doringo, and Ruben Bong Bylon. The protesters raised placards and chanted slogans calling for the release of political prisoners, rejection of the proposed Pax Silica initiative, the fight against imperialism, and genuine agrarian reform. The groups also demanded the immediate release of the nine activists arrested during Sunday's anti-ASEAN protests, whom they claimed were illegally detained. The demonstration followed another gathering outside the MPD headquarters on Wednesday, Nov. 18, when several protesters gathered near the police compound's gate to air grievances over the arrests. On Thursday, authorities closed the compound's gate as MPD personnel positioned themselves at the entrance to prevent the protesters from entering the premises. Ines also said those arrested would be detained and their cases would be decided by the court if they were found to have committed violations of the Revised Penal Code. Ines maintained that the matter should be addressed through proper legal processes while encouraging the protesters to communicate their concerns peacefully.

results.title: Valenzuela gov't adopts one-ID policy for city transactions
results.description: Valenzuela City residents are now required to present only one valid government-issued identification card (ID) for transactions requiring identity verification at city government offices. Mayor Weslie “Wes” Gatchalian signed Executive Order No. 2026-151 on Nov. 9 to simplify government transactions and reduce processing time for residents. The policy applies to both in-person and online transactions with city government offices where identity verification is required. Under the order, residents may present one valid government-issued ID in physical or electronic format, provided it bears their photograph and signature. "Where identity verification is required by law or the applicable Citizen's Charter, the office shall accept one (1) valid government-issued ID under the subsequent sections," Section 1 of the executive order states. Accepted IDs include the Philippine National ID, passport, driver's license, Professional Regulation Commission ID, Integrated Bar of the Philippines ID, National Bureau of Investigation clearance, police clearance, postal ID, and voter's ID or certification. Other accepted documents include the Government Service Insurance System e-card, Social Security System card, PhilHealth ID, senior citizen ID or booklet, Overseas Workers Welfare Administration ID, Overseas Filipino Worker ID, seaman's book, and alien certificate of registration. Government office IDs, persons with disability IDs or booklets, Department of Social Welfare and Development certifications, solo parent IDs, Tax Identification Number IDs, Unified Multi-Purpose ID cards, and residency IDs issued by local government units are also recognized. However, city government offices may still request additional identification when required by law or when discrepancies or concerns about an ID's authenticity cannot be resolved. In such cases, residents must first be given a chance to explain the discrepancy or present another valid ID. Any request for additional identification must also be approved by the concerned office head or an authorized supervisor. The order also requires city government offices to protect residents' personal information during identity verification. "Offices shall inspect or authenticate the ID and process only the personal data necessary for the transaction," Section 4 states. The provision also requires compliance with Republic Act No. 10173, or the Data Privacy Act of 2012, when collecting, copying, or retaining identification information. The executive order took effect immediately upon its issuance on Nov. 9. The city government said the policy aims to remove unnecessary documentary requirements and make public services faster and more convenient for residents.
